bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cong demands regular pay scale for unfunded school teachers, takes out 'kafan' march
bihar_raw_news.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Bihar Cong demands regular pay scale for unfunded school teachers, takes out... India Bihar Cong demands regular pay scale for unfunded school teachers, takes out ‘kafan’ march PTI 05 September, 2026 09:48 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 5 (PTI) The Bihar Congress took out a “kafan march” here on Saturday demanding that the BJP government in the state provide teachers of non-funded educational institutes with a regular pay scale, which would ensure them a stable income. Leaders claimed that several party workers, who had participated in the march from Patna’s Gandhi Maidan to the Shaheed Smarak near the Bihar Assembly on Teachers’ Day, were detained by police midway. Patna Town SDPO Kamakhya Narayan Singh said 13 protestors were detained during the march and later released. Show Full Article In a statement, the party said the protest march was taken out under the aegis of the Congress Seva Dal, a grassroots frontal volunteer organisation, to protest against the state’s 1981 Non-Funded Education Policy. The policy was modified by the Nitish Kumar-led government in 2008 to usher in a performance-based grant system. Under it, the Bihar government provides post-result grants to private or community-run educational institutions that largely sustain on students’ fees. The staff of these institutes do not have a regular pay scale, leading to unstable income. The protestors demanded that the government immediately resolve the problems of teachers of those educational institutes, take a positive decision on their demands and eliminate inequality in the education system, it added. Bihar Congress Seva Dal president Sanjay Yadav demanded a regular pay scale for the teachers in place of grants. “We took out the ‘kafan yatra’, demanding the Bihar chief minister provide us at least a shroud. Before elections, then chief minister (Nitish Kumar) had assured us of a pay scale for such teachers, but neither he nor his successor could provide us that,” he said. The Congress claimed that Yadav and other party leaders, including Afroz Alam, Rajesh Rathore and Ruchi Singh, along with hundreds of protestors, were detained by police. Earlier in the day, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, while addressing a gathering at Patna’s SK Memorial Hall on the occasion of Teachers’ Day, said the government was contemplating a new pay scale for teachers of unfunded schools by combining the internal resources of non-aided institutions and the government’s grants. “We have decided to create a new system to combine their internal resources and the government’s grants to create a new pay scale, which will ensure justice for unfunded teachers,” he said. The Congress’ Bihar in-charge Krishna Allavaru accused the government of “trying to suppress the voice of teachers” and said detaining teachers and their leaders on Teachers’ Day was an “insult to democratic values”. “The government should resolve the problems of teachers. But instead of listening to them, it is adopting a repressive approach,” Allavaru said. PTI SUK

bihar_raw_news.title: " Bihar to develop around 700 model schools for NEET, JEE preparation": CM Samrat Choudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: "Bihar to develop around 700 model schools for NEET, JEE preparation": CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Sep 05, 2026 20:13 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 5 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday announced that around 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan Model Schools will be developed across the state to provide students with facilities and academic support for competitive examinations such as NEET and JEE. Addressing the Teacher's Day occasion 2026 at Sri Krishna Memorial Hall here, Choudhary said the proposed university would provide regular training to teachers from primary education to higher education, engineering and polytechnic institutions. "More than seven lakh teachers are working in Bihar from primary schools to higher education, engineering and polytechnic institutions. To improve the quality of teachers and provide them regular training, a separate Teacher Training University will be established," the Chief Minister said. Choudhary also announced that Bihar will develop a modern artificial intelligence ecosystem in collaboration with leading technology companies such as Google, Microsoft and Sarvam AI. "Teachers will be provided training in the latest artificial intelligence technologies," he said. An MoU was signed between the Bihar Education Department and Google during the programme for training teachers in AI and modern technologies. The Chief Minister said efforts would also be made to establish a centre of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Bihar to provide better higher education opportunities to students. On examination reforms, Choudhary said the government aims to release matriculation examination results within seven days of completion of the examination. Students dissatisfied with their marks would be allowed to reappear within 15 days in designated examination slots, he said. He added that arrangements were being developed to release engineering and polytechnic results within 24 hours. A committee headed by a sitting High Court judge has been constituted to suggest structural reforms in the examination system, Choudhary said, adding that the government would act on its recommendations. The state is also considering decentralising the examination system and releasing results centre-wise to reduce delays and facilitate timely admissions, he said. The Chief Minister said, "Around 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan Model Schools would be developed in Bihar, where students would receive facilities to prepare for competitive examinations such as NEET and JEE." Live online teachers would be made available to students, including those staying in hostels and those commuting from home, enabling them to access academic assistance round the clock, he said. On Bihar's educational heritage, Choudhary said the process of establishing the historic Vikramshila University was being taken forward. "The land acquisition process for Vikramshila University was completed on July 15, and work to take the project forward on the ground will be undertaken within the next year," he said. Highlighting improvements in school education, Choudhary said the primary-level dropout rate declined from around 46 per cent in 2004-05 to 2 per cent in 2024-25. bihar_raw_news.title: Prior consent mandatory for CBI to probe offences involving public servants: Bihar govt
bihar_raw_news.content: ANI CBI will now need to seek prior permission from the Bihar government before conducting any investigation involving officers or employees of the state government, according to a notification issued by the Home Department (Police Branch) under the Bihar Government Patna: The Bihar government on Saturday asserted that obtaining prior consent shall be "mandatory" for the Central Bureau of Investigation to probe offences allegedly involving public servants in the state. This has been made clear in a Home Department notification, which has been stated to be "in supersession of all previous notifications on this subject". Also Read: VHP bars participation of Muslims in garba, dandiya events in Maharashtra; sets rules for organisers "The governor of Bihar hereby accords consent to extension of the powers and jurisdiction of members of Delhi Police Special Establishment throughout the state...for the investigation of offences..... allegedly committed by employees of the Government of India, Public Sector Undertakings and private individuals under direct control of Government of India", said the notification. Notably, the CBI is a non-statutory body that derives its powers from the Delhi Police Special Establishment Act , 1946. Live Events The Home department notification added that it shall be "mandatory to obtain the prior consent of Government of Bihar" in cases where the offences "involve public servants appointed in connection with the affairs of Government of Bihar or persons appointed in connection with the affairs of any corporation, company or bank owned and controlled by the Government of Bihar or any institution receiving or having received financial assistance from the Government of Bihar". bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Mandates Pre-Approval for CBI Probes Involving State Officials - Devdiscourse
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Mandates Pre-Approval for CBI Probes Involving State Officials The Bihar government now requires the CBI to secure prior permission to investigate state officers, as per a recent notification. This development marks a significant shift, demanding individual approval for each case involving the state's apparatus, while aligning with the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. Devdiscourse News Desk | Updated: 05-09-2026 13:05 IST | Created: 05-09-2026 13:05 IST Representative Image (File Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI Country: India SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... In a notable policy shift, the Bihar government has declared that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) must obtain prior consent before conducting any investigations involving its state officers or employees. This directive, as per the Home Department's notification, was issued in the Governor of Bihar's name and hinges on Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. The notification elaborates on the circumstances under which CBI's investigatory consent is granted generally, such as offences involving Central Government employees, Public Sector Undertakings, and specific private individuals. Yet, it stipulates that when Bihar's public servants or state-controlled entities are implicated, the state's explicit consent is mandatory. This stipulation ensures localized oversight, with the state evaluating investigatory permissions on a case-by-case basis, upon receipt of a proposal from the Delhi Special Police Establishment. Historically, the CBI's authority originated from the Special Police Establishment formed in 1941, tasked with probing wartime bribe and corruption charges in India. The crucial Delhi Special Police Establishment Act of 1946 empowered the CBI to investigate central corruption cases, a mandate now navigated with additional procedural layers in Bihar. national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu today said that a Viksit Bharat will only be possible with quality education. Addressing the National Teachers Award ceremony 2026 in New Delhi on the occasion of Teachers’ Day, the President said that a society that respects its teachers is a progressive society in the right sense. She asserted that education is the most effective means of realising the ideal of equality of opportunity enshrined in our Constitution. She said that the achievement of a negligible primary school dropout rate has been made possible through the efforts of teachers. President Murmu added that academic excellence, skill development and entrepreneurship play a crucial role in the development of the nation. The President noted that establishing India as the Skill Capital of the World, alongside becoming a Knowledge Power, is the priority of the country. Highlighting the importance of knowledge as the greatest source of power, she said that education empowers individuals to think independently, make informed decisions and contribute meaningfully to the progress of the nation. The President said that dedicated teachers are the frontline nation builders. The President also recalled Savitribai Phule’s pivotal role in advancing women’s rights and education. President Murmu said that school education forms the foundation of education system. She added that by diligently focusing on the intellectual, physical, and moral development of children in the early grades, teachers can prepare future generations of excellent students and dutiful citizens. The President underlined that many students come from economically disadvantaged families, who are first-generation learners, or who transition from ordinary village schools to large city schools. She said some are naturally shy, some possess immense talent but lack self-confidence, and some are children with special needs. She noted that it is the special responsibility of teachers to instil confidence in them and uplift all such students who, for any reason, feel a sense of inadequacy. President Murmu today conferred the National Teachers Awards. 48 selected school teachers from 27 States, seven Union Territories and six Organizations of the Central Government received the awards. The President also presented National Awards to 21 teachers and faculty members of Higher Education Institutions and polytechnics. Twelve teachers and faculty members from central Higher Education Institutions, five from state universities, including three government and two private colleges and four from polytechnics, including two government and two private polytechnics, have been selected for the Awards. Short documentaries on each awardee depicting the exemplary work done by them were showcased at the event. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Ministers of State for Education Jayant Singh and Dr Sukanta Majumdar, Secretary School Education T K Anil Kumar, Secretary Higher Education Dipti Gaur Mukherjee and Secretary Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Debashree Mukherjee were present on the occasion.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 203 PM Modi urges teachers to go beyond textbooks while shaping lives of students
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called upon teachers to go beyond textbooks and play a greater role in preserving childhood while shaping the lives of students. He made these remarks while interacting with the National Teachers’ Day Award winners in New Delhi yesterday. While sharing glimpses of the interaction with Teachers in a social media post, the Prime Minister emphasised that teachers must ensure that the child within every student remains alive, and for that, they should also preserve the child within themselves. He stressed that bringing about real change in children requires teachers to become a part of their lives rather than limiting themselves to the syllabus. Highlighting key health and social issues, Mr Modi expressed concern over excessive screen time among children and suggested encouraging sports, outdoor activities and creative pursuits as effective ways to reduce screen addiction. He also spoke about breast cancer awareness, saying that women are increasingly coming forward voluntarily for health check-ups, reflecting growing awareness. The Prime Minister cautioned against the growing menace of drug abuse, saying awareness must be created continuously, as children may unknowingly fall prey to such substances. Mr Modi also referred to the National Education Policy and stressed the importance of taking children outside the classroom and connecting them with real-world skills and forms of work. This year, 82 teachers and educators have been selected for the National Teachers Awards from three departments. These include 48 teachers from the Department of School Education and Literacy, 21 teachers and faculty members from Higher Educational Institutions and Polytechnics, and 13 skill trainers from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. The awardees highlighted the experiences and innovations that have shaped their teaching journey. They shared several creative approaches adopted by them to make classroom learning more engaging and effective. The Prime Minister further underlined that Teachers’ Day is about appreciating the strong contribution of teachers to our society, and noted that it is also a day to pay homage to Bharat Ratna Dr S Radhakrishnan.

national_raw_news.title: Manipur CM attends Teachers’ Day celebrations at City Convention Centre in Imphal 4 hours ago 61
national_raw_news.content: Manipur today joined the rest of the country in observing Teachers’ Day. The state-level celebration, organised by the State Education Department at the City Convention Centre, Imphal, was attended by Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand and newly appointed Chief Secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur as Chief Guest and President, respectively. During the function, seven teachers were presented with this year’s State Teachers’ Awards 2026, recognising their contributions to student enrolment, preventing school dropouts, and introducing innovative teaching methodologies. DM College of Teacher Education Associate Professor Kh. Dineshkumar and the team behind “Building and Learning Aid” (BaLa) were awarded appreciation certificates. Three colleges received the “Educational Excellence Award”, carrying cash prizes of 5 lakh rupees, 3 lakh rupees, and 2 lakh rupees, respectively. Five colleges were also awarded cash prizes of Rupees 1 lakh each as consolation prizes. Speaking on the occasion, Khemchand said, “A teacher’s biggest virtue is their ability to treat all the students in their class as their own family members.” He also lauded the students of TG Higher Secondary School and CC Higher Secondary School for withdrawing their support for the general strike called by some CSOs demanding the NRC before the census. Shri Khemchand urged individuals and CSOs to come forward for talks and negotiations before launching such agitations, as the poorest sections are the worst affected. Chief Secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur expressed his appreciation for initiatives such as those undertaken by BaLa. He urged the award-winning teachers to continue their pursuit of excellence and not rest on their laurels.
